newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Four Bosnian Serbs jailed for "spying" on Croats.
newsitem.headline: Four Bosnian Serbs jailed for "spying" on Croats.

text.p: Four Bosnian Serb civilians have been jailed for 27 days in Croat-controlled Bosnia for allegedly spying on a Croat militia base, the United Nations said on Thursday.

The four were sentenced on Wednesday in the northeastern town of Orasje a day after being detained by Bosnian Croat militia, a spokesman for the U.N. police monitoring force (IPTF) in post-war Bosnia said. Two other Serbs were freed after questioning.

Spokesman Andrea Angeli said the Serbs told the IPTF they were stopped after losing their way while crossing Croat-held territory between the Bosnian Serb towns of Bijeljina and Bosanski Brod in the ethnically-divided country.

"There was a lot of fog and they took the road to (Croat-controlled) Odzak. Somewhere near Donja Dubica they stopped a car to check their map. They met HVO (Croat militia) soldiers who ordered the Serbs to follow them," he said.
The Serbs' cars and vehicles were checked at a nearby Croat camp and nothing illegal was found but the Croats released only two Serbs after questioning, Angeli told Reuters.
The U.N. police were told that the other Serbs went before a Croat court and were sentenced to 27 days in prison "for observing a military installation of the 4th HVO Motorised Brigade".
"IPTF was able to see them (jailed Serbs) yesterday afternoon and they are OK," said Angeli.
The Serbs told the U.N. police they were from the southern town of Trebinje at the other end of Bosnia.
